headline: CPI at 8:30 with September a literal coin flip; US Navy fires on a blockade runner and Brent nears $90
client_frame:
July CPI lands at 8:30 this morning into the tightest possible setup. A live CME pull (cohort 8/11) now has the September FOMC at **hold 50.4% vs hike 49.6%** — a genuine coin flip, eased back from the 53.4% hike lean we reported yesterday. CNN independently described the market as roughly 50/50. So this print does not merely inform the September decision; it plausibly decides it.

Consensus is headline **+0.1% MoM / +3.4% YoY** and core **+0.2% / +2.5%**, with core point estimates clustering +0.20-0.22% and a right tail from Wells Fargo (+0.24%) and Deutsche Bank (+0.26%). Worth remembering that June headline actually *fell* 0.4% MoM, so the bar for a benign-looking rebound is low. The asymmetry is what matters: with September balanced on a knife edge and Cleveland's Hammack saying Monday that 'some number' of additional hikes may be needed and that a single 25bp move 'probably doesn't do a whole lot,' a hot core has far more room to reprice the front end than a soft one has to soothe it. Then $42B of 10-year notes prices at 1:00 pm, hours after the number.

Against that, the AI complex just delivered. SMCI, CoreWeave, and Lumentum all beat and guided higher, and futures are firmer because of it — NQ +0.65%. But oil keeps grinding: Brent settled $88.91 and trades near $89.70 after a US Navy helicopter disabled a containership trying to run the blockade of Iranian ports. Equities fell about a third of a percent Tuesday while VIX also fell, which is not fear — it is a market that has hedged and is waiting.

Chip melt-up — Samsung +7.7%, SK Hynix +7.1%. Single-source (AP wire); large move, treat as indicative
Direction confirmed across three sources (-0.9% to -1.2%); exact level varies

single_name_moves.note: Revenue $11.12B MISSED (~$11.6B est) on customer power/cooling delays, but adj EPS $1.70 crushed ~$0.85 est and FY27 revenue guided $65-72B vs ~$53.1B consensus. Gross margin +800bp YoY to 17.5%. Sources span +7% to +9%.

UP SHARPLY, magnitude UNRESOLVED (+7% to +18% across sources). Revenue $2.575B +112%, beat; net loss -$1.14 vs -$1.41 est; backlog $104B +46% plus $25B new Q3 commitments; FY26 guide raised to $12.4-13.2B. Capex guide $35-39B and interest expense $640M vs $267M are the offsets.

CONTRADICTORY after-hours reads (flat to +6.5%), consistent with spike-then-fade. Revenue $1.006B +109%, non-GAAP EPS $3.23 beat ~$2.98, Q1 guide $1.225-1.275B (+130% YoY) — but a $7.8B non-cash charge produced a $7.2B GAAP net loss.
Revenue $365.4M beat, same-restaurant sales +9.0% (traffic +5.3%), EPS $0.19 beat. Note guidance was REAFFIRMED, not raised, and restaurant margin fell 60bp to 25.7%.
Tuesday's worst notable single-name move (Polygon-verified from $38.78)

geo_headlines: **CPI today 8:30 ET.** Headline +0.1% MoM / +3.4% YoY, core +0.2% / +2.5% consensus. Core estimates cluster +0.20-0.22%; Wells Fargo +0.24% and Deutsche Bank +0.26% form the right tail. June headline fell 0.4% MoM, per Reuters.
**September is a coin flip.** Live CME (cohort 8/11): hold **50.4%** vs hike **49.6%**, eased from 53.4% hike-favored the prior day. Fed funds band 3.50-3.75%.

**Hammack, Monday: hawkish.** Cleveland's president said 'some number' of additional rate hikes may be needed and that a single 25bp move 'probably doesn't do a whole lot.' She speaks again tomorrow 8:15 ET, with Barkin at 8:40.

**ESCALATION: a US Navy MH-60 fired two Hellfire missiles** at the Panama-flagged containership *Vela Nova* in the Gulf of Oman, ~71nm off Pakistan, disabling its steering and engine room after it tried to breach the blockade of Iranian ports. CENTCOM cumulative through 8/11: 55 vessels redirected, 3 disabled, 2 boarded.
**Oil keeps climbing.** Tuesday settles WTI **$83.20 (+1.3%)**, Brent **$88.91 (+1.4%)**. Wednesday ~7am: WTI ~$83.96, Brent ~$89.69 — Brent within a dollar of $90 and up roughly 15% in a week.

**Bab el-Mandeb attack:** a Houthi strike on a cargo ship Tuesday killed four crew plus two rescuers, per the body of the Reuters report (its headline says three — inconsistency flagged, not resolved).

**Still no Hormuz reopening.** No sign the Aug 5 Iran-Oman route understanding has cleared Supreme Leader sign-off. JMIC's transit-volume series and CENTCOM's enforcement counts measure different things and should not be conflated.
**$42B 10-year auction today at 1:00 pm ET** — pricing hours after CPI. $25B 30-year follows Thursday alongside PPI.
**Canada tariff deadline Aug 19** (threatened 50%, would cover USMCA goods). Russia sanctions bill passed the Senate 86-11; House vote expected next month.
**Credit still shows no stress** — spreads tight and risk-on, no widening through the oil move.
**UNVERIFIED:** an API crude build of +9.07M barrels vs an expected ~500k draw is circulating from an aggregator only. No top-tier confirmation found; EIA's official number is at 10:30 ET.
